remove-vanished string A semicolon-separated list of things to remove when they or the user vanishes during a sync. The following values are possible: 'entry' removes the user/group when not returned from the sync. 'properties' removes the set properties on existing user/group that do not appear in the source (even custom ones). 'acl' removes acls when the user/group is not returned from the sync. Instead of a list it also can be 'none' (the default).
scope string Select what to sync. users groups both
dry-run boolean If set, does not write anything.

all.description: Backup all known guest systems on this host.

enabled.description: Enable or disable the job.

exclude-path.description: Exclude certain files/directories (shell globs). Paths starting with '/' are anchored to the container's root, other paths match relative to each subdirectory.

enabled.description: Enable backup fleecing. Cache backup data from blocks where new guest writes happen on specified storage instead of copying them directly to the backup target. This can help guest IO performance and even prevent hangs, at the cost of requiring more storage space.

storage.description: Use this storage to storage fleecing images. For efficient space usage, it's best to use a local storage that supports discard and either thin provisioning or sparse files.

ionice.description: Set IO priority when using the BFQ scheduler. For snapshot and suspend mode backups of VMs, this only affects the compressor. A value of 8 means the idle priority is used, otherwise the best-effort priority is used with the specified value.

lockwait.description: Maximal time to wait for the global lock (minutes).

mailnotification.description: Deprecated: use notification targets/matchers instead. Specify when to send a notification mail

mailto.description: Deprecated: Use notification targets/matchers instead. Comma-separated list of email addresses or users that should receive email notifications.

mode.description: Backup mode.

next-run.description: UNIX timestamp when this backup job will be executed next

node.description: Only run if executed on this node.

notes-template.description: Template string for generating notes for the backup(s). It can contain variables which will be replaced by their values. Currently supported are {{cluster}}, {{guestname}}, {{node}}, and {{vmid}}, but more might be added in the future. Needs to be a single line, newline and backslash need to be escaped as '\n' and '\\' respectively.

notification-mode.description: Determine which notification system to use. If set to 'legacy-sendmail', vzdump will consider the mailto/mailnotification parameters and send emails to the specified address(es) via the 'sendmail' command. If set to 'notification-system', a notification will be sent via PVE's notification system, and the mailto and mailnotification will be ignored. If set to 'auto' (default setting), an email will be sent if mailto is set, and the notification system will be used if not.

pbs-change-detection-mode.description: PBS mode used to detect file changes and switch encoding format for container backups.

max-workers.description: Applies to VMs. Allow up to this many IO workers at the same time.

pbs-entries-max.description: Applies to container backups sent to PBS. Limits the number of entries allowed in memory at a given time to avoid unintended OOM situations. Increase it to enable backups of containers with a large amount of files.

pigz.description: Use pigz instead of gzip when N>0. N=1 uses half of cores, N>1 uses N as thread count.

pool.description: Backup all known guest systems included in the specified pool.

protected.description: If true, mark backup(s) as protected.

prune-backups.description: Use these retention options instead of those from the storage configuration.

keep-all.description: Keep all backups. Conflicts with the other options when true.

keep-daily.description: Keep backups for the last <N> different days. If there is morethan one backup for a single day, only the latest one is kept.

keep-hourly.description: Keep backups for the last <N> different hours. If there is morethan one backup for a single hour, only the latest one is kept.

keep-monthly.description: Keep backups for the last <N> different months. If there is morethan one backup for a single month, only the latest one is kept.

keep-weekly.description: Keep backups for the last <N> different weeks. If there is morethan one backup for a single week, only the latest one is kept.

keep-yearly.description: Keep backups for the last <N> different years. If there is morethan one backup for a single year, only the latest one is kept.

repeat-missed.description: If true, the job will be run as soon as possible if it was missed while the scheduler was not running.

schedule.description: Backup schedule. The format is a subset of `systemd` calendar events.

stop.description: Stop running backup jobs on this host.

stopwait.description: Maximal time to wait until a guest system is stopped (minutes).

storage.description: Store resulting file to this storage.

tmpdir.description: Store temporary files to specified directory.

vmid.description: The ID of the guest system you want to backup.

zstd.description: Zstd threads. N=0 uses half of the available cores, if N is set to a value bigger than 0, N is used as thread count.

failback.description: Automatically migrate HA resource to the node with the highest priority according to their node affinity  rules, if a node with a higher priority than the current node comes online.

max_relocate.description: Maximal number of resource relocate tries when a resource fails to start.

sid.description: HA resource ID. This consists of a resource type followed by a resource specific name, separated with colon (example: vm:100 / ct:100). For virtual machines and containers, you can simply use the VM or CT id as a shortcut (example: 100).

state.description: Requested resource state.
state.verbose_description:
Requested resource state. The CRM reads this state and acts accordingly.
Please note that `enabled` is just an alias for `started`.

`started`;;

The CRM tries to start the resource. Service state is
set to `started` after successful start. On node failures, or when start
fails, it tries to recover the resource.  If everything fails, service
state it set to `error`.

`stopped`;;

The CRM tries to keep the resource in `stopped` state, but it
still tries to relocate the resources on node failures.

`disabled`;;

The CRM tries to put the resource in `stopped` state, but does not try
to relocate the resources on node failures. The main purpose of this
state is error recovery, because it is the only way to move a resource out
of the `error` state.

`ignored`;;

The resource gets removed from the manager status and so the CRM and the LRM do
not touch the resource anymore. All {pve} API calls affecting this resource
will be executed, directly bypassing the HA stack. CRM commands will be thrown
away while the resource is in this state. The resource will not get relocated
on node failures.

ha.verbose_description:
Configures how the HA Manager should select nodes to start or recover services:

- with 'basic', only the number of services is used,
- with 'static', static CPU and memory configuration of services are considered,
- with 'dynamic', static and dynamic CPU and memory usage of services are considered.

ha-auto-rebalance.description: Whether to use CRS for balancing HA resources automatically depending on the current node imbalance.

ha-auto-rebalance-hold-duration.description: The number of HA rounds for which the cluster node imbalance threshold must be exceeded before triggering an automatic resource balancing migration.

ha-auto-rebalance-margin.description: The minimum relative improvement in cluster node imbalance, in percent, to commit to a resource balancing migration.

ha-auto-rebalance-method.description: The method to use for the scoring of balancing migrations.

ha-auto-rebalance-threshold.description: The cluster node imbalance, in percent, which will trigger the automatic resource balancing system if exceeded.

shutdown_policy.description: The policy for HA services on node shutdown. 'freeze' disables auto-recovery, 'failover' ensures recovery, 'conditional' recovers on poweroff and freezes on reboot. 'migrate' will migrate running services to other nodes, if possible. With 'freeze' or 'failover', HA Services will always get stopped first on shutdown.
shutdown_policy.verbose_description: Describes the policy for handling HA services on poweroff or reboot of a node. Freeze will always freeze services which are still located on the node on shutdown, those services won't be recovered by the HA manager. Failover will not mark the services as frozen and thus the services will get recovered to other nodes, if the shutdown node does not come up again quickly (< 1min). 'conditional' chooses automatically depending on the type of shutdown, i.e., on a reboot the service will be frozen but on a poweroff the service will stay as is, and thus get recovered after about 2 minutes. Migrate will try to move all running services to another node when a reboot or shutdown was triggered. The poweroff process will only continue once no running services are located on the node anymore. If the node comes up again, the service will be moved back to the previously powered-off node, at least if no other migration, reloaction or recovery took place.

You're allowed to use this in local networks, i.e., those not directly reachable by the public (e.g., in a LAN or behind NAT).
mac_prefix.verbose_description:
Prefix for the auto-generated MAC addresses of virtual guests. The default `BC:24:11` is the Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI) assigned by the IEEE to Proxmox Server Solutions GmbH for a MAC Address Block Large (MA-L). You're allowed to use this in local networks, i.e., those not directly reachable by the public (e.g., in a LAN or NAT/Masquerading).
 
Note that when you run multiple cluster that (partially) share the networks of their virtual guests, it's highly recommended that you extend the default MAC prefix, or generate a custom (valid) one, to reduce the chance of MAC collisions. For example, add a separate extra hexadecimal to the Proxmox OUI for each cluster, like `BC:24:11:0` for the first, `BC:24:11:1` for the second, and so on.
 Alternatively, you can also separate the networks of the guests logically, e.g., by using VLANs.

For publicly accessible guests it's recommended that you get your own https://standards.ieee.org/products-programs/regauth/[OUI from the IEEE] registered or coordinate with your, or your hosting providers, network admins.

Control how often the daily update job should send out notifications:
* 'auto' daily for systems with a valid subscription, as those are assumed to be  production-ready and thus should know about pending updates.
* 'always' every update, if there are new pending updates.
* 'never' never send a notification for new pending updates.

user-allow.description: Controls tag usage for users without `Sys.Modify` on `/` by either allowing `none`, a `list`, already `existing` or anything (`free`).
user-allow.verbose_description:
Controls which tags can be set or deleted on resources a user controls (such as guests). Users with the `Sys.Modify` privilege on `/` are alwaysunrestricted.
* 'none' no tags are usable.
* 'list' tags from 'user-allow-list' are usable.
* 'existing' like list, but already existing tags of resources are also usable.
* 'free' no tag restrictions.

flags.description: List of additional CPU flags separated by ';'. Use '+FLAG' to enable, '-FLAG' to disable a flag. There is a special 'nested-virt' shorthand which controls nested virtualization for the current CPU ('svm' for AMD and 'vmx' for Intel). Custom CPU models can specify any flag supported by QEMU/KVM, VM-specific flags must be from the following set for security reasons: aes, amd-no-ssb, amd-ssbd, hv-evmcs, hv-tlbflush, ibpb, md-clear, nested-virt, pcid, pdpe1gb, spec-ctrl, ssbd, virt-ssbd

guest-phys-bits.description: Number of physical address bits available to the guest.

hidden.description: Do not identify as a KVM virtual machine. Only affects vCPUs with x86-64 architecture.

hv-vendor-id.description: The Hyper-V vendor ID. Some drivers or programs inside Windows guests need a specific ID.

level.description: Maximum input value for the basic CPUID leaves the guest can query - that is the vendor (leaf 0), family/model/stepping and feature bits (leaf 1), cache and topology info (leaves 4 and B), and so on. Higher-numbered leaves are hidden. Setting '30' is a common workaround for Hyper-V boot failures on Windows guests running on recent Intel hosts. Only applies when the vCPU architecture is x86_64.

phys-bits.description: The physical memory address bits that are reported to the guest OS. Should be smaller or equal to the host's. Set to 'host' to use value from host CPU, but note that doing so will break live migration to CPUs with other values.

reported-model.description: CPU model and vendor to report to the guest. Must be a QEMU/KVM supported model. Only valid for custom CPU model definitions, default models will always report themselves to the guest OS.

searchText:
POST
/cluster/sdn/zones
cluster
create
Create a new sdn zone object.
type string Plugin type. evpn faucet qinq simple vlan vxlan
zone string The SDN zone object identifier.
advertise-subnets boolean Advertise IP prefixes (Type-5 routes) instead of MAC/IP pairs (Type-2 routes).
bridge string The bridge for which VLANs should be managed.
bridge-disable-mac-learning boolean Disable auto mac learning.
controller string Controller for this zone.
dhcp string Type of the DHCP backend for this zone dnsmasq
disable-arp-nd-suppression boolean Suppress IPv4 ARP && IPv6 Neighbour Discovery messages.
dns string dns api server
dnszone string dns domain zone  ex: mydomain.com
dp-id integer Faucet dataplane id
exitnodes string List of cluster node names.
exitnodes-local-routing boolean Allow exitnodes to connect to EVPN guests.
exitnodes-primary string Force traffic through this exitnode first.
fabric string SDN fabric to use as underlay for this VXLAN zone.
ipam string use a specific ipam
lock-token string the token for unlocking the global SDN configuration
mac string Anycast logical router mac address.
mtu integer MTU of the zone, will be used for the created VNet bridges.
nodes string List of cluster node names.
peers string Comma-separated list of peers, that are part of the VXLAN zone. Usually the IPs of the nodes.
reversedns string reverse dns api server
rt-import string List of Route Targets that should be imported into the VRF of the zone.
secondary-controllers array Additional controllers.
tag integer Service-VLAN Tag (outer VLAN)
vlan-protocol string Which VLAN protocol should be used for the creation of the QinQ zone. 802.1q 802.1ad
vrf-vxlan integer VNI for the zone VRF.
vxlan-port integer UDP port that should be used for the VXLAN tunnel (default 4789).

idmap.description: Map specific container UIDs/GIDs to underlying disk UIDs/GIDs for this mount point
idmap.verbose_description:
Customize UID/GID mappings that override the container's `lxc.idmap` for this mount point. Accepts a semicolon-separated list of `type:container:disk:range-size` entries.

`type` is `u` for UID or `g` for GID.

`container` is the first ID as seen inside the container.

`disk` is the first corresponding ID on the underlying filesystem.

`range-size` is the number of consecutive IDs to map.

Unmapped IDs fall back to the container's `lxc.idmap`.

Example 1: `u:123:456:1` maps UID 123 in the container to UID 456 on the disk. Files owned by UID 456 on the disk will appear as UID 123 inside the container.

Example 2: `g:100:50:5` maps 5 consecutive GIDs, such that GIDs 100-104 in the container are mapped to GIDs 50-54 on the disk.

Example 3: `passthrough` identity-maps all UIDs and GIDs, meaning IDs inside the container will match the IDs on the disk.

idmap.description: Map specific container UIDs/GIDs to underlying disk UIDs/GIDs for this mount point
idmap.verbose_description:
Customize UID/GID mappings that override the container's `lxc.idmap` for this mount point. Accepts a semicolon-separated list of `type:container:disk:range-size` entries.

`type` is `u` for UID or `g` for GID.

`container` is the first ID as seen inside the container.

`disk` is the first corresponding ID on the underlying filesystem.

`range-size` is the number of consecutive IDs to map.

Unmapped IDs fall back to the container's `lxc.idmap`.

Example 1: `u:123:456:1` maps UID 123 in the container to UID 456 on the disk. Files owned by UID 456 on the disk will appear as UID 123 inside the container.

Example 2: `g:100:50:5` maps 5 consecutive GIDs, such that GIDs 100-104 in the container are mapped to GIDs 50-54 on the disk.

Example 3: `passthrough` identity-maps all UIDs and GIDs, meaning IDs inside the container will match the IDs on the disk.

acl.description: Explicitly enable or disable ACL support.

idmap.description: Map specific container UIDs/GIDs to underlying disk UIDs/GIDs for this mount point
idmap.verbose_description:
Customize UID/GID mappings that override the container's `lxc.idmap` for this mount point. Accepts a semicolon-separated list of `type:container:disk:range-size` entries.

`type` is `u` for UID or `g` for GID.

`container` is the first ID as seen inside the container.

`disk` is the first corresponding ID on the underlying filesystem.

`range-size` is the number of consecutive IDs to map.

Unmapped IDs fall back to the container's `lxc.idmap`.

Example 1: `u:123:456:1` maps UID 123 in the container to UID 456 on the disk. Files owned by UID 456 on the disk will appear as UID 123 inside the container.

Example 2: `g:100:50:5` maps 5 consecutive GIDs, such that GIDs 100-104 in the container are mapped to GIDs 50-54 on the disk.

Example 3: `passthrough` identity-maps all UIDs and GIDs, meaning IDs inside the container will match the IDs on the disk.

quota.description: Enable user quotas inside the container (not supported with zfs subvolumes)

replicate.description: Will include this volume to a storage replica job.

shared.description: Mark this non-volume mount point as available on multiple nodes (see 'nodes')
shared.verbose_description:
Mark this non-volume mount point as available on all nodes.

WARNING: This option does not share the mount point automatically, it assumes it is shared already!

size.description: Volume size (read only value).

volume.description: Volume, device or directory to mount into the container.

searchdomain.description: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if you neither set searchdomain nor nameserver.

startup.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped.

swap.description: Amount of SWAP for the container in MB.

tags.description: Tags of the Container. This is only meta information.

template.description: Enable/disable Template.

timezone.description: Time zone to use in the container. If option isn't set, then nothing will be done. Can be set to 'host' to match the host time zone, or an arbitrary time zone option from /usr/share/zoneinfo/zone.tab

tty.description: Specify the number of tty available to the container

unprivileged.description: Makes the container run as unprivileged user. For creation, the default is 1. For restore, the default is the value from the backup. (Should not be modified manually.)

description: Create or restore a virtual machine.

requestParameters.name: vmid
requestParameters.description: The (unique) ID of the VM.

requestParameters.name: acpi
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable ACPI.

requestParameters.name: affinity
requestParameters.description: List of host cores used to execute guest processes, for example: 0,5,8-11

requestParameters.name: agent
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable communication with the QEMU Guest Agent and its properties.

requestParameters.name: allow-ksm
requestParameters.description: Allow memory pages of this guest to be merged via KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging).

requestParameters.name: amd-sev
requestParameters.description: Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) features by AMD CPUs

requestParameters.name: arch
requestParameters.description: Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture.

requestParameters.name: archive
requestParameters.description: The backup archive. Either the file system path to a .tar or .vma file (use '-' to pipe data from stdin) or a proxmox storage backup volume identifier.

requestParameters.name: args
requestParameters.description: Arbitrary arguments passed to kvm.

requestParameters.name: audio0
requestParameters.description: Configure a audio device, useful in combination with QXL/Spice.

requestParameters.name: autostart
requestParameters.description: Automatic restart after crash (currently ignored).

requestParameters.name: balloon
requestParameters.description: Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero.

requestParameters.name: bios
requestParameters.description: Select BIOS implementation.

requestParameters.name: boot
requestParameters.description: Specify guest boot order. Use the 'order=' sub-property as usage with no key or 'legacy=' is deprecated.

requestParameters.name: bootdisk
requestParameters.description: Enable booting from specified disk. Deprecated: Use 'boot: order=foo;bar' instead.

requestParameters.name: bwlimit
requestParameters.description: Override I/O bandwidth limit (in KiB/s).
requestParameters.default: restore limit from datacenter or storage config

requestParameters.name: cdrom
requestParameters.description: This is an alias for option -ide2

requestParameters.name: cicustom
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Specify custom files to replace the automatically generated ones at start.

requestParameters.name: cipassword
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords.

requestParameters.name: citype
requestParameters.description: Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows.

requestParameters.name: ciupgrade
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: do an automatic package upgrade after the first boot.

requestParameters.name: ciuser
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user.

requestParameters.name: cores
requestParameters.description: The number of cores per socket.

requestParameters.name: cpu
requestParameters.description: Emulated CPU type.

requestParameters.name: cpulimit
requestParameters.description: Limit of CPU usage.

requestParameters.name: cpuunits
requestParameters.description: CPU weight for a VM, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2.

requestParameters.name: description
requestParameters.description: Description for the VM. Shown in the web-interface VM's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

requestParameters.name: efidisk0
requestParameters.description: Configure a disk for storing EFI vars. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and that the default EFI vars are copied to the volume instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: force
requestParameters.description: Allow to overwrite existing VM.

requestParameters.name: freeze
requestParameters.description: Freeze CPU at startup (use 'c' monitor command to start execution).

requestParameters.name: ha-managed
requestParameters.description: Add the VM as a HA resource after it was created.

requestParameters.name: hookscript
requestParameters.description: Script that will be executed during various steps in the vms lifetime.

requestParameters.name: hostpci[n]
requestParameters.description: Map host PCI devices into guest.

requestParameters.name: hotplug
requestParameters.description: Selectively enable hotplug features. This is a comma separated list of hotplug features: 'network', 'disk', 'cpu', 'memory', 'usb' and 'cloudinit'. Use '0' to disable hotplug completely. Using '1' as value is an alias for the default `network,disk,usb`. USB hotplugging is possible for guests with machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7.

requestParameters.name: hugepages
requestParameters.description:
Enables hugepages memory.

Sets the size of hugepages in MiB. If the value is set to 'any' then 1 GiB hugepages will be used if possible, otherwise the size will fall back to 2 MiB.

requestParameters.name: ide[n]
requestParameters.description: Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: import-working-storage
requestParameters.description: A file-based storage with 'images' content-type enabled, which is used as an intermediary extraction storage during import. Defaults to the source storage.

requestParameters.name: intel-tdx
requestParameters.description: Trusted Domain Extension (TDX) features by Intel CPUs

requestParameters.name: ipconfig[n]
requestParameters.description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

requestParameters.name: ivshmem
requestParameters.description: Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host.

requestParameters.name: keephugepages
requestParameters.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.

requestParameters.name: keyboard
requestParameters.description: Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS.

requestParameters.name: kvm
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable KVM hardware virtualization.

requestParameters.name: live-restore
requestParameters.description: Start the VM immediately while importing or restoring in the background.

requestParameters.name: localtime
requestParameters.description: Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS.

requestParameters.name: lock
requestParameters.description: Lock/unlock the VM.

requestParameters.name: machine
requestParameters.description: Specify the QEMU machine.

requestParameters.name: memory
requestParameters.description: Memory properties.

requestParameters.name: migrate_downtime
requestParameters.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU).

requestParameters.name: migrate_speed
requestParameters.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.

requestParameters.name: name
requestParameters.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

requestParameters.name: nameserver
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

requestParameters.name: net[n]
requestParameters.description: Specify network devices.

requestParameters.name: numa
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable NUMA.

requestParameters.name: numa[n]
requestParameters.description: NUMA topology.

requestParameters.name: onboot
requestParameters.description: Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup.

requestParameters.name: ostype
requestParameters.description: Specify guest operating system.

requestParameters.name: parallel[n]
requestParameters.description: Map host parallel devices (n is 0 to 2).

requestParameters.name: pool
requestParameters.description: Add the VM to the specified pool.

requestParameters.name: protection
requestParameters.description: Sets the protection flag of the VM. This will disable the remove VM and remove disk operations.

requestParameters.name: reboot
requestParameters.description: Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot.

requestParameters.name: rng0
requestParameters.description: Configure a VirtIO-based Random Number Generator.

requestParameters.name: sata[n]
requestParameters.description: Use volume as SATA hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 5). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: scsi[n]
requestParameters.description: Use volume as SCSI hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 30). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: scsihw
requestParameters.description: SCSI controller model

requestParameters.name: searchdomain
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

requestParameters.name: serial[n]
requestParameters.description: Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3)

requestParameters.name: shares
requestParameters.description: Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd.

requestParameters.name: smbios1
requestParameters.description: Specify SMBIOS type 1 fields.

requestParameters.name: smp
requestParameters.description: The number of CPUs. Please use option -sockets instead.

requestParameters.name: sockets
requestParameters.description: The number of CPU sockets.

requestParameters.name: spice_enhancements
requestParameters.description: Configure additional enhancements for SPICE.

requestParameters.name: sshkeys
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).

requestParameters.name: start
requestParameters.description: Start VM after it was created successfully.

requestParameters.name: startdate
requestParameters.description: Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are:'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'.

requestParameters.name: startup
requestParameters.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped.

requestParameters.name: storage
requestParameters.description: Default storage.

requestParameters.name: tablet
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable the USB tablet device.

requestParameters.name: tags
requestParameters.description: Tags of the VM. This is only meta information.

requestParameters.name: tdf
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable time drift fix.

requestParameters.name: template
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable Template.

requestParameters.name: tpmstate0
requestParameters.description: Configure a Disk for storing TPM state. The format is fixed to 'raw'. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and 4 MiB will be used instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: unique
requestParameters.description: Assign a unique random ethernet address.

requestParameters.name: unused[n]
requestParameters.description: Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually.

requestParameters.name: usb[n]
requestParameters.description: Configure an USB device (n is 0 to 4, for machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7, n can be up to 14).

requestParameters.name: vcpus
requestParameters.description: Number of hotplugged vcpus.

requestParameters.name: vga
requestParameters.description: Configure the VGA hardware.

requestParameters.name: virtio[n]
requestParameters.description: Use volume as VIRTIO hard disk (n is 0 to 15). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: virtiofs[n]
requestParameters.description: Configuration for sharing a directory between host and guest using Virtio-fs.

requestParameters.name: vmgenid
requestParameters.description: Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly.

requestParameters.name: vmstatestorage
requestParameters.description: Default storage for VM state volumes/files.

requestParameters.name: watchdog
requestParameters.description: Create a virtual hardware watchdog device.

permissions.description: You need 'VM.Allocate' permissions on /vms/{vmid} or on the VM pool /pool/{pool}. For restore (option 'archive'), it is enough if the user has 'VM.Backup' permission and the VM already exists. If you create disks you need 'Datastore.AllocateSpace' on any used storage.If you use a bridge/vlan, you need 'SDN.Use' on any used bridge/vlan.

raw.description: Create or restore a virtual machine.
raw.name: create_vm

affinity.description: List of host cores used to execute guest processes, for example: 0,5,8-11

agent.description: Enable/disable communication with the QEMU Guest Agent and its properties.

enabled.description: Enable/disable communication with a QEMU Guest Agent (QGA) running in the VM.

freeze-fs.description: Freeze guest filesystems through QGA for consistent disk state on operations such as snapshots, backups, replications and clones.
freeze-fs.verbose_description:
Whether to issue the guest-fsfreeze-freeze and guest-fsfreeze-thaw QEMU guest agent commands. Backups in snapshot mode, clones, snapshots without RAM, importing disks from a running guest, and replications normally issue a guest-fsfreeze-freeze and a respective thaw command when the QEMU Guest agent option is enabled in the guest's configuration and the agent is running inside of the guest.

The deprecated 'freeze-fs-on-backup' setting is treated as an alias for this setting.

fstrim_cloned_disks.description: Run fstrim after moving a disk or migrating the VM.

allow-ksm.description: Allow memory pages of this guest to be merged via KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging).

amd-sev.description: Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) features by AMD CPUs

arch.description: Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture.

archive.description: The backup archive. Either the file system path to a .tar or .vma file (use '-' to pipe data from stdin) or a proxmox storage backup volume identifier.

args.verbose_description:
Arbitrary arguments passed to kvm, for example:

args: -no-reboot -smbios 'type=0,vendor=FOO'

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

size.description: The size of the file in MB.

keephugepages.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.

live-restore.description: Start the VM immediately while importing or restoring in the background.

localtime.description: Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS.

aw-bits.description: Specifies the vIOMMU address space bit width.
aw-bits.verbose_description:
Specifies the vIOMMU address space bit width.

Intel vIOMMU supports a bit width of either 39 or 48 bits and VirtIO vIOMMU supports any bit width between 32 and 64 bits.

enable-s3.description: Enables S3 power state. Defaults to false beginning with machine types 9.2+pve1, true before.

enable-s4.description: Enables S4 power state. Defaults to false beginning with machine types 9.2+pve1, true before.

viommu.description: Enable and set guest vIOMMU variant (Intel vIOMMU needs q35 to be set as machine type).

current.description: Current amount of online RAM for the VM in MiB. This is the maximum available memory when you use the balloon device.

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU).

migrate_speed.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.

name.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

nameserver.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique within your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.
macaddr.verbose_description: A common MAC address with the I/G (Individual/Group) bit not set.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

mtu.description: Force MTU of network device (VirtIO only). Setting to '1' or empty will use the bridge MTU

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

ostype.verbose_description:

optimization/features for specific operating systems:

[horizontal]
other;; unspecified OS
wxp;; Microsoft Windows XP
w2k;; Microsoft Windows 2000
w2k3;; Microsoft Windows 2003
w2k8;; Microsoft Windows 2008
wvista;; Microsoft Windows Vista
win7;; Microsoft Windows 7
win8;; Microsoft Windows 8/2012/2012r2
win10;; Microsoft Windows 10/2016/2019
win11;; Microsoft Windows 11/2022/2025
l24;; Linux 2.4 Kernel
l26;; Linux 2.6 - 7.X Kernel
solaris;; Solaris/OpenSolaris/OpenIndiania kernel

You can also run without any graphic card, using a serial device as terminal.

vmgenid.verbose_description:
The VM generation ID (vmgenid) device exposes a 128-bit integer value identifier to the guest OS. This allows to notify the guest operating system when the virtual machine is executed with a different configuration (e.g. snapshot execution or creation from a template). The guest operating system notices the change, and is then able to react as appropriate by marking its copies of distributed databases as dirty, re-initializing its random number generator, etc.
Note that auto-creation only works when done through API/CLI create or update methods, but not when manually editing the config file.

searchText:
POST
/nodes/{node}/qemu
nodes
create_vm
Create or restore a virtual machine.
node string The cluster node name.
vmid integer The (unique) ID of the VM.
acpi boolean Enable/disable ACPI.
affinity string List of host cores used to execute guest processes, for example: 0,5,8-11
agent string Enable/disable communication with the QEMU Guest Agent and its properties.
allow-ksm boolean Allow memory pages of this guest to be merged via KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging).
amd-sev string Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) features by AMD CPUs
arch string Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture. x86_64 aarch64
archive string The backup archive. Either the file system path to a .tar or .vma file (use '-' to pipe data from stdin) or a proxmox storage backup volume identifier.
args string Arbitrary arguments passed to kvm.
audio0 string Configure a audio device, useful in combination with QXL/Spice.
autostart boolean Automatic restart after crash (currently ignored).
balloon integer Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero.
bios string Select BIOS implementation. seabios ovmf
boot string Specify guest boot order. Use the 'order=' sub-property as usage with no key or 'legacy=' is deprecated.
bootdisk string Enable booting from specified disk. Deprecated: Use 'boot: order=foo;bar' instead.
bwlimit integer Override I/O bandwidth limit (in KiB/s).
cdrom string This is an alias for option -ide2
cicustom string cloud-init: Specify custom files to replace the automatically generated ones at start.
cipassword string cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords.
citype string Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows. configdrive2 nocloud opennebula
ciupgrade boolean cloud-init: do an automatic package upgrade after the first boot.
ciuser string cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user.
cores integer The number of cores per socket.
cpu string Emulated CPU type.
cpulimit number Limit of CPU usage.
cpuunits integer CPU weight for a VM, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2.
description string Description for the VM. Shown in the web-interface VM's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.
efidisk0 string Configure a disk for storing EFI vars. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and that the default EFI vars are copied to the volume instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.
force boolean Allow to overwrite existing VM.
freeze boolean Freeze CPU at startup (use 'c' monitor command to start execution).
ha-managed boolean Add the VM as a HA resource after it was created.
hookscript string Script that will be executed during various steps in the vms lifetime.
hostpci[n] string Map host PCI devices into guest.
hotplug string Selectively enable hotplug features. This is a comma separated list of hotplug features: 'network', 'disk', 'cpu', 'memory', 'usb' and 'cloudinit'. Use '0' to disable hotplug completely. Using '1' as value is an alias for the default `network,disk,usb`. USB hotplugging is possible for guests with machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7.
hugepages string Enables hugepages memory.

Sets the size of hugepages in MiB. If the value is set to 'any' then 1 GiB hugepages will be used if possible, otherwise the size will fall back to 2 MiB. any 2 1024
ide[n] string Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.
import-working-storage string A file-based storage with 'images' content-type enabled, which is used as an intermediary extraction storage during import. Defaults to the source storage.
intel-tdx string Trusted Domain Extension (TDX) features by Intel CPUs
ipconfig[n] string cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.
ivshmem string Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host.
keephugepages boolean Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.
keyboard string Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS. de de-ch da en-gb en-us es fi fr fr-be fr-ca fr-ch hu is it ja lt mk nl no pl pt pt-br sv sl tr
kvm boolean Enable/disable KVM hardware virtualization.
live-restore boolean Start the VM immediately while importing or restoring in the background.
localtime boolean Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS.
lock string Lock/unlock the VM. backup clone create migrate rollback snapshot snapshot-delete suspending suspended
machine string Specify the QEMU machine.
memory string Memory properties.
migrate_downtime number Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU).
migrate_speed integer Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.
name string Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.
nameserver string cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.
net[n] string Specify network devices.
numa boolean Enable/disable NUMA.
numa[n] string NUMA topology.
onboot boolean Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup.
ostype string Specify guest operating system. other wxp w2k w2k3 w2k8 wvista win7 win8 win10 win11 l24 l26 solaris
parallel[n] string Map host parallel devices (n is 0 to 2).
pool string Add the VM to the specified pool.
protection boolean Sets the protection flag of the VM. This will disable the remove VM and remove disk operations.
reboot boolean Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot.
rng0 string Configure a VirtIO-based Random Number Generator.
sata[n] string Use volume as SATA hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 5). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.
scsi[n] string Use volume as SCSI hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 30). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.
scsihw string SCSI controller model lsi lsi53c810 virtio-scsi-pci virtio-scsi-single megasas pvscsi
searchdomain string cloud-init: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.
serial[n] string Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3)
shares integer Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd.
smbios1 string Specify SMBIOS type 1 fields.
smp integer The number of CPUs. Please use option -sockets instead.
sockets integer The number of CPU sockets.
spice_enhancements string Configure additional enhancements for SPICE.
sshkeys string cloud-init: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).
start boolean Start VM after it was created successfully.
startdate string Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are:'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'.
startup string Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped.
storage string Default storage.
tablet boolean Enable/disable the USB tablet device.
tags string Tags of the VM. This is only meta information.
tdf boolean Enable/disable time drift fix.
template boolean Enable/disable Template.
tpmstate0 string Configure a Disk for storing TPM state. The format is fixed to 'raw'. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and 4 MiB will be used instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.
unique boolean Assign a unique random ethernet address.
unused[n] string Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually.
usb[n] string Configure an USB device (n is 0 to 4, for machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7, n can be up to 14).
vcpus integer Number of hotplugged vcpus.
vga string Configure the VGA hardware.
virtio[n] string Use volume as VIRTIO hard disk (n is 0 to 15). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.
virtiofs[n] string Configuration for sharing a directory between host and guest using Virtio-fs.
vmgenid string Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly.
vmstatestorage string Default storage for VM state volumes/files.
watchdog string Create a virtual hardware watchdog device.

agent.description: Enable/disable communication with the QEMU Guest Agent and its properties.

freeze-fs.description: Freeze guest filesystems through QGA for consistent disk state on operations such as snapshots, backups, replications and clones.
freeze-fs.verbose_description:
Whether to issue the guest-fsfreeze-freeze and guest-fsfreeze-thaw QEMU guest agent commands. Backups in snapshot mode, clones, snapshots without RAM, importing disks from a running guest, and replications normally issue a guest-fsfreeze-freeze and a respective thaw command when the QEMU Guest agent option is enabled in the guest's configuration and the agent is running inside of the guest.

The deprecated 'freeze-fs-on-backup' setting is treated as an alias for this setting.

arch.description: Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture.

args.verbose_description:

args: -no-reboot -smbios 'type=0,vendor=FOO'

NOTE: this option is for experts only.

balloon.description: Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero.

cipassword.description: cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords.

citype.description: Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows.

ciuser.description: cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user.

cores.description: The number of cores per socket.

cpulimit.verbose_description:

NOTE: If the computer has 2 CPUs, it has total of '2' CPU time. Value '0' indicates no CPU limit.

cpuunits.verbose_description: CPU weight for a VM. Argument is used in the kernel fair scheduler. The larger the number is, the more CPU time this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all the other running VMs.

The value '2023k' means that the 'Microsoft UEFI CA 2023', the 'Windows UEFI CA 2023' and the 'Microsoft Corporation KEK 2K CA 2023' certificates are included. The values '2023' and '2023w' are deprecated and for compatibility only.

pre-enrolled-keys.description: Use am EFI vars template with distribution-specific and Microsoft Standard keys enrolled, if used with 'efitype=4m'. Note that this will enable Secure Boot by default, though it can still be turned off from within the VM.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU).

nameserver.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadecimal numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such
machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

Either this or the 'mapping' key must be set.

mapping.description: The ID of a cluster wide mapping. Either this or the default-key 'host' must be set.

usb3.description: Specifies whether if given host option is a USB3 device or port. For modern guests (machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 and windows > 7), this flag is irrelevant (all devices are plugged into a xhci controller).

vga.verbose_description:

Since QEMU 2.9 the default VGA display type is 'std' for all OS types besides some Windows versions (XP and older) which use 'cirrus'. The 'qxl' option enables the SPICE display server. For win* OS you can select how many independent displays you want, Linux guests can add displays them self.
You can also run without any graphic card, using a serial device as terminal.

vmgenid.description: Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly.
vmgenid.verbose_description:
The VM generation ID (vmgenid) device exposes a 128-bit integer value identifier to the guest OS. This allows to notify the guest operating system when the virtual machine is executed with a different configuration (e.g. snapshot execution or creation from a template). The guest operating system notices the change, and is then able to react as appropriate by marking its copies of distributed databases as dirty, re-initializing its random number generator, etc.
Note that auto-creation only works when done through API/CLI create or update methods, but not when manually editing the config file.

watchdog.verbose_description: Create a virtual hardware watchdog device. Once enabled (by a guest action), the watchdog must be periodically polled by an agent inside the guest or else the watchdog will reset the guest (or execute the respective action specified)

freeze-fs.verbose_description:
Whether to issue the guest-fsfreeze-freeze and guest-fsfreeze-thaw QEMU guest agent commands. Backups in snapshot mode, clones, snapshots without RAM, importing disks from a running guest, and replications normally issue a guest-fsfreeze-freeze and a respective thaw command when the QEMU Guest agent option is enabled in the guest's configuration and the agent is running inside of the guest.

The deprecated 'freeze-fs-on-backup' setting is treated as an alias for this setting.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

mtu.description: Force MTU of network device (VirtIO only). Setting to '1' or empty will use the bridge MTU

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadecimal numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such
machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

Either this or the 'mapping' key must be set.

mapping.description: The ID of a cluster wide mapping. Either this or the default-key 'host' must be set.

usb3.description: Specifies whether if given host option is a USB3 device or port. For modern guests (machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 and windows > 7), this flag is irrelevant (all devices are plugged into a xhci controller).

clipboard.description: Enable a specific clipboard. If not set, depending on the display type the SPICE one will be added. Live migration with a VNC clipboard is not possible with QEMU machine version < 10.1.

memory.description: Sets the VGA memory (in MiB). Has no effect with serial display.

type.description: Select the VGA type. Using type 'cirrus' is not recommended.

vga.verbose_description:
Configure the VGA Hardware. If you want to use high resolution modes (>= 1280x1024x16) you may need to increase the vga memory option. Since QEMU 2.9 the default VGA display type is 'std' for all OS types besides some Windows versions (XP and older) which use 'cirrus'. The 'qxl' option enables the SPICE display server. For win* OS you can select how many independent displays you want, Linux guests can add displays them self.
You can also run without any graphic card, using a serial device as terminal.

snapshot.description: Controls qemu's snapshot mode feature. If activated, changes made to the disk are temporary and will be discarded when the VM is shutdown.

virtiofs[n].description: Configuration for sharing a directory between host and guest using Virtio-fs.

cache.description: The caching policy the file system should use (auto, always, metadata, never).

direct-io.description: Honor the O_DIRECT flag passed down by guest applications.

dirid.description: Mapping identifier of the directory mapping to be shared with the guest. Also used as a mount tag inside the VM.

expose-acl.description: Enable support for POSIX ACLs (enabled ACL implies xattr) for this mount.

expose-xattr.description: Enable support for extended attributes for this mount.

vmgenid.description: Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly.
vmgenid.verbose_description:
The VM generation ID (vmgenid) device exposes a 128-bit integer value identifier to the guest OS. This allows to notify the guest operating system when the virtual machine is executed with a different configuration (e.g. snapshot execution or creation from a template). The guest operating system notices the change, and is then able to react as appropriate by marking its copies of distributed databases as dirty, re-initializing its random number generator, etc.
Note that auto-creation only works when done through API/CLI create or update methods, but not when manually editing the config file.

vmstate.description: Reference to a volume which stores the VM state. This is used internally for snapshots.

vmstatestorage.description: Default storage for VM state volumes/files.

watchdog.description: Create a virtual hardware watchdog device.
watchdog.verbose_description: Create a virtual hardware watchdog device. Once enabled (by a guest action), the watchdog must be periodically polled by an agent inside the guest or else the watchdog will reset the guest (or execute the respective action specified)

requestParameters.name: autostart
requestParameters.description: Automatic restart after crash (currently ignored).

requestParameters.name: background_delay
requestParameters.description: Time to wait for the task to finish. We return 'null' if the task finish within that time.

requestParameters.name: balloon
requestParameters.description: Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero.

requestParameters.name: bios
requestParameters.description: Select BIOS implementation.

requestParameters.name: boot
requestParameters.description: Specify guest boot order. Use the 'order=' sub-property as usage with no key or 'legacy=' is deprecated.

requestParameters.name: bootdisk
requestParameters.description: Enable booting from specified disk. Deprecated: Use 'boot: order=foo;bar' instead.

requestParameters.name: cdrom
requestParameters.description: This is an alias for option -ide2

requestParameters.name: cicustom
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Specify custom files to replace the automatically generated ones at start.

requestParameters.name: cipassword
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords.

requestParameters.name: citype
requestParameters.description: Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows.

requestParameters.name: ciupgrade
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: do an automatic package upgrade after the first boot.

requestParameters.name: ciuser
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user.

requestParameters.name: cores
requestParameters.description: The number of cores per socket.

requestParameters.name: cpu
requestParameters.description: Emulated CPU type.

requestParameters.name: cpulimit
requestParameters.description: Limit of CPU usage.

requestParameters.name: cpuunits
requestParameters.description: CPU weight for a VM, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2.

requestParameters.name: delete
requestParameters.description: A list of settings you want to delete.

requestParameters.name: description
requestParameters.description: Description for the VM. Shown in the web-interface VM's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

requestParameters.name: digest
requestParameters.description: Prevent changes if current configuration file has different SHA1 digest. This can be used to prevent concurrent modifications.

requestParameters.name: efidisk0
requestParameters.description: Configure a disk for storing EFI vars. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and that the default EFI vars are copied to the volume instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: force
requestParameters.description: Force physical removal. Without this, we simple remove the disk from the config file and create an additional configuration entry called 'unused[n]', which contains the volume ID. Unlink of unused[n] always cause physical removal.

requestParameters.name: freeze
requestParameters.description: Freeze CPU at startup (use 'c' monitor command to start execution).

requestParameters.name: hookscript
requestParameters.description: Script that will be executed during various steps in the vms lifetime.

requestParameters.name: hostpci[n]
requestParameters.description: Map host PCI devices into guest.

requestParameters.name: hotplug
requestParameters.description: Selectively enable hotplug features. This is a comma separated list of hotplug features: 'network', 'disk', 'cpu', 'memory', 'usb' and 'cloudinit'. Use '0' to disable hotplug completely. Using '1' as value is an alias for the default `network,disk,usb`. USB hotplugging is possible for guests with machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7.

requestParameters.name: hugepages
requestParameters.description:
Enables hugepages memory.

Sets the size of hugepages in MiB. If the value is set to 'any' then 1 GiB hugepages will be used if possible, otherwise the size will fall back to 2 MiB.

requestParameters.name: ide[n]
requestParameters.description: Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: import-working-storage
requestParameters.description: A file-based storage with 'images' content-type enabled, which is used as an intermediary extraction storage during import. Defaults to the source storage.

requestParameters.name: intel-tdx
requestParameters.description: Trusted Domain Extension (TDX) features by Intel CPUs

requestParameters.name: ipconfig[n]
requestParameters.description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit
gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires
cloud-init 19.4 or newer.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using
dhcp on IPv4.

requestParameters.name: ivshmem
requestParameters.description: Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host.

requestParameters.name: keephugepages
requestParameters.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts.

requestParameters.name: keyboard
requestParameters.description: Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS.

requestParameters.name: kvm
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable KVM hardware virtualization.

requestParameters.name: localtime
requestParameters.description: Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS.

requestParameters.name: lock
requestParameters.description: Lock/unlock the VM.

requestParameters.name: machine
requestParameters.description: Specify the QEMU machine.

requestParameters.name: memory
requestParameters.description: Memory properties.

requestParameters.name: migrate_downtime
requestParameters.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU).

requestParameters.name: migrate_speed
requestParameters.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.

requestParameters.name: name
requestParameters.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

requestParameters.name: nameserver
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

requestParameters.name: net[n]
requestParameters.description: Specify network devices.

requestParameters.name: numa
requestParameters.description: Enable/disable NUMA.

requestParameters.name: numa[n]
requestParameters.description: NUMA topology.

requestParameters.name: onboot
requestParameters.description: Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup.

requestParameters.name: ostype
requestParameters.description: Specify guest operating system.

requestParameters.name: parallel[n]
requestParameters.description: Map host parallel devices (n is 0 to 2).

requestParameters.name: protection
requestParameters.description: Sets the protection flag of the VM. This will disable the remove VM and remove disk operations.

requestParameters.name: reboot
requestParameters.description: Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot.

requestParameters.name: revert
requestParameters.description: Revert a pending change.

requestParameters.name: rng0
requestParameters.description: Configure a VirtIO-based Random Number Generator.

requestParameters.name: sata[n]
requestParameters.description: Use volume as SATA hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 5). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume.

requestParameters.name: scsihw
requestParameters.description: SCSI controller model

requestParameters.name: searchdomain
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

requestParameters.name: serial[n]
requestParameters.description: Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3)

requestParameters.name: shares
requestParameters.description: Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd.

requestParameters.name: skiplock
requestParameters.description: Ignore locks - only root is allowed to use this option.

requestParameters.name: smbios1
requestParameters.description: Specify SMBIOS type 1 fields.

requestParameters.name: smp
requestParameters.description: The number of CPUs. Please use option -sockets instead.

requestParameters.name: sockets
requestParameters.description: The number of CPU sockets.

requestParameters.name: spice_enhancements
requestParameters.description: Configure additional enhancements for SPICE.

requestParameters.name: sshkeys
requestParameters.description: cloud-init: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).

requestParameters.name: startdate
requestParameters.description: Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are:'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'.

requestParameters.name: startup
requestParameters.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. aw-bits.verbose_description:
Specifies the vIOMMU address space bit width.

Intel vIOMMU supports a bit width of either 39 or 48 bits and VirtIO vIOMMU supports any bit width between 32 and 64 bits.

enable-s3.description: Enables S3 power state. Defaults to false beginning with machine types 9.2+pve1, true before.

enable-s4.description: Enables S4 power state. Defaults to false beginning with machine types 9.2+pve1, true before.

viommu.description: Enable and set guest vIOMMU variant (Intel vIOMMU needs q35 to be set as machine type).

current.description: Current amount of online RAM for the VM in MiB. This is the maximum available memory when you use the balloon device.

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU).

migrate_speed.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.

name.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

nameserver.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique within your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.
macaddr.verbose_description: A common MAC address with the I/G (Individual/Group) bit not set.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

mtu.description: Force MTU of network device (VirtIO only). Setting to '1' or empty will use the bridge MTU

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

memory.description: Amount of memory this NUMA node provides.

onboot.description: Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup.

ostype.verbose_description:
Specify guest operating system. This is used to enable special
optimization/features for specific operating systems:

[horizontal]
other;; unspecified OS
wxp;; Microsoft Windows XP
w2k;; Microsoft Windows 2000
w2k3;; Microsoft Windows 2003
w2k8;; Microsoft Windows 2008
wvista;; Microsoft Windows Vista
win7;; Microsoft Windows 7
win8;; Microsoft Windows 8/2012/2012r2
win10;; Microsoft Windows 10/2016/2019
win11;; Microsoft Windows 11/2022/2025
l24;; Linux 2.4 Kernel
l26;; Linux 2.6 - 7.X Kernel
solaris;; Solaris/OpenSolaris/OpenIndiania kernel

Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3), and pass through a
host serial device (i.e. /dev/ttyS0), or create a unix socket on the
host side (use 'qm terminal' to open a terminal connection).

NOTE: If you pass through a host serial device, it is no longer possible to migrate such machines -
